newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Petrol shortage hits teeming Nigerian city.
newsitem.headline: Petrol shortage hits teeming Nigerian city.

text.p: A new bout of petrol shortage hit Nigeria's biggest city Lagos on Monday following revelations that a key oil refinery had been closed.
"The queues for petrol are building up rapidly and it seems to be panic buying because of the announcement that Warri refinery is shut," said an attendant at a station in central Lagos.
Oil Minister Dan Etete was quoted by newspapers at the weekend as saying the oil refinery in the midwestern city of Warri had been shut following ethnic clashes which recently rocked the city.

The semi-official Daily Times said Etete disclosed this when military leaders met him on Thursday at the refinery to discuss the clashes which swept Warri in response to the relocation of local council headquarters.
The minister said the refinery, which supplies western Nigeria, had to be closed when its storage tanks became full and vessels were unable to sail into Warri to load oil products.
Warri refinery has the capacity to process 125,000 barrels of crude daily into oil products.
"Up until yesterday people were buying fuel without problem but today there are queues because everybody wants to fill up," said one taxi driver.
Nigeria, Africa's leading oil-producing nation, is often hit by petrol shortage because of the poor management of its four refineries and inadequate distribution of products.
The last shortage ended only three weeks ago.
